text:
[LCDB.3.3.3] **Composition across bound facts.** When a rule
binds more than one fact, the activation key is the ordered
concatenation, per bound pattern in source order, of each
fact's contributing slots:

- a `logical` fact contributes its declared `key` slots. A
  schema whose key is ∅ (every slot `mutable`) contributes
  nothing, so a single-pattern rule on such a schema is
  rule-global (the `AmbientTemp{ts mutable, celsius mutable}`
  case);
- a `ttl` / event fact carries no identity markers
  ([LFAC.1.7.6]) and contributes nothing on its own. A rule that
  binds one and carries a rate modifier must declare its key with
  `by:` ([LCDB.3.3.4]);
- when no bound fact contributes a slot, the key is empty and
  the cooldown is rule-global.

idris.name: Lcdb_3_3_3__fact
idris.note: One bound fact as role-value pairs, zipped rather than two lists so a role and its value cannot drift apart -- the failure this clause is about is a key that says less than the author thinks, and a model able to mis-pair them could reproduce it for the wrong reason. Restricted to the logical branch, as `Lcdb_3_3_3__slot` is.

idris.name: Lcdb_3_3_3__slot
idris.note: Two identity roles, not three, and that is the clause's logical-fact branch only. A ttl/event fact takes the other branch entirely -- it carries no identity markers ([LFAC.1.7.6]), contributes nothing on its own, and a rate-limited rule binding it keys on its `by:` paths ([LCDB.3.3.4]) -- which this type cannot express. `mutable` is what "everything that is not `key`" is called, not a third role.

idris.name: lcdb_3_3_3__a_keyed_schema_separates
idris.note: THE FALSIFIABILITY CONTROL, without which the theorem above is worthless: a schema WITH a key slot separates activations that differ in it. Stated from an arbitrary inequality, so it is the general property rather than one pair that happens to differ.

idris.name: lcdb_3_3_3__all_mutable_contributes_nothing
idris.note: A schema whose key is empty contributes nothing, quantified over the value list rather than shown on the two-slot example -- "every slot `mutable`" is a property of schemas of any width.

idris.name: lcdb_3_3_3__ambient_temp
idris.note: `AmbientTemp{ts mutable, celsius mutable}` -- the clause's own worked example, as a function of both values so a theorem about it covers every activation of that rule rather than one reading.

idris.name: lcdb_3_3_3__ambient_temp_key_is_empty
idris.note: The clause's example has the empty key whatever it binds.

idris.name: lcdb_3_3_3__contributes
idris.note: "A `logical` fact contributes its declared `key` slots", verbatim and complete for that branch: key slots in declaration order, mutable slots dropped.

idris.name: lcdb_3_3_3__every_activation_shares_one_key
idris.note: Any two activations of that rule share one activation key, quantified over both readings of both. Suppression is keyed on (rule, activation_key), so one key for every activation IS one window for the whole rule. THIS IS EVIDENCE FOR REFUTING [LCDB.7.2](a) AND NOT THE VERDICT: `refuted` is asserted-only per clause.schema.json, and taking it is the coordinator's. It says nothing about [LCDB.7.2](b), the grammar claim, which holds.

idris.name: lcdb_3_3_3__key
idris.note: The ordered concatenation per bound pattern in source order. Complete over logical facts and silent about ttl/event ones, so it is the clause's key composition restricted to the branch the two types above model.

idris.name: lcdb_3_3_3__mutable_does_not_enter_the_key
idris.note: A mutable slot beside a key one does not weaken it, so a churning value cannot reset a window -- [LCDB.3.3.1]'s guarantee as a consequence of this clause's composition. A tuple of all LHS binding values would destroy exactly this.

idris.name: Lcdb_3_2_1__cool
idris.note: LESS than the clause: the composition across bound facts -- per positive pattern in source order, a logical schema's declared key slots in declaration order -- is the fixture lowering's (scripts/idris_lower.py, as dsc.rete.m's `key_vars` composes it), and Lcdb/RuleGlobal.idr holds its theorems for the logical branch; here the key is a function of the match. The empty key, when no bound fact contributes, is `lcdb_3_3_3__empty_key`.

idris.name: lcdb_3_3_3__cool_perkey
idris.note: Two activations of one rule with different keys cool independently: both fire in one pump. Executed, rgate.cool_perkey's schedule.

idris.name: lcdb_3_3_3__empty_key
idris.note: 'When no bound fact contributes a slot, the key is empty': the code of the empty tuple, one for every match -- the rule-global cooldown.

idris.name: lcdb_3_3_3__empty_key_is_rule_global
idris.note: THE EMPTY KEY IS RULE-GLOBAL: under it two facts in one pump share one window and the second is refused. Executed.

idris.name: lcdb_3_3_3__key_separates
idris.note: A second key inside the first key's window fires: the window is the key's. Executed, rgate.key_separates's schedule.
